7	Each configuration uses a balanced corpus of 500 texts per depth level (generations 0--5).
8	We organize results around four questions:
9	(1)~Does $\Kempirical = 2$ hold across configurations?
10	(2)~Do depth classifiers transfer across models?
11	(3)~Is the feature degradation ordering model-independent?
12	(4)~How does generation mode affect detectability?
13	
14	%% ====================================================================
15	\subsection{$\Kstar = 2$ Across All Configurations}
16	\label{sec:kstar_boundary}
17	
18	Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} reports pairwise $\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs
19	across all four configurations, with bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals
20	(1{,}000 resamples) and permutation-test $p$-values for the critical 1v2
21	and 2v3 boundaries.
22	
23	\begin{table}[t]
24	\centering
25	\small
26	\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs.  Bootstrap 95\% CIs
27	and permutation $p$-values shown for the $\Kstar$ boundary rows (1v2,
28	2v3).  $\Kempirical = 2$ requires 1v2 $\text{CI}_\text{low} > \theta$
29	and 2v3 $\text{CI}_\text{high} < \theta$ with $\theta = 0.60$.
30	All 0v1 permutation $p = 0.002$.}
31	\label{tab:kstar_ci}
32	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
33	\toprule
34	 & Qwen-rw & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-cont \\
35	\midrule
36	0v1 & 0.9956 & 0.9932 & 0.9970 & 0.9972 \\[4pt]
37	1v2 & 0.6955 & 0.6539 & 0.6145 & 0.6112 \\
38	{\footnotesize CI}
39	  & {\footnotesize [.6859,\,.7041]}
40	  & {\footnotesize [.6454,\,.6630]}

44	  & {\footnotesize .002}
45	  & {\footnotesize .002}
46	  & {\footnotesize .002}
47	  & {\footnotesize .002} \\[4pt]
48	2v3 & 0.5893 & 0.5514 & 0.5496 & 0.5609 \\
49	{\footnotesize CI}
50	  & {\footnotesize [.5795,\,.5991]}
51	  & {\footnotesize [.5417,\,.5628]}
52	  & {\footnotesize [.5399,\,.5596]}
53	  & {\footnotesize [.5511,\,.5712]} \\
54	{\footnotesize $p$}
55	  & {\footnotesize .002}
56	  & {\footnotesize .002}
57	  & {\footnotesize .002}

59	3v4 & 0.5435 & 0.5152 & 0.5091 & 0.5409 \\

62	\end{tabular}

65	The pattern is uniform across all four configurations:
66	0v1 discrimination is near-perfect ($\auc > 0.99$),
67	followed by a sharp drop at 1v2 ($\auc$ range: 0.6112--0.6955),
68	with 2v3 falling below the decision threshold $\theta = 0.60$
69	($\auc$ range: 0.5496--0.5893).
70	All subsequent pairs (3v4, 4v5) converge toward chance.
71	Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay} visualizes this decay.
72	
73	\begin{figure}[t]
74	\centering
75	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_auc_decay.pdf}
76	\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ as a function of depth pair across four model
77	configurations.  All configurations show a sharp drop between 0v1 and
78	1v2, with 2v3 and deeper pairs falling below the decision threshold
79	$\theta = 0.60$ (dashed line).  Error bars: bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
80	\label{fig:auc_decay}
81	\end{figure}
82	
83	For the $\Kstar$ determination, all four 1v2 CI lower bounds exceed
84	$\theta$: Qwen-rw ($\text{CI}_\text{low} = 0.6859$), Pythia (0.6454),
85	OLMo (0.6045), and Qwen-cont (0.6015).
86	Conversely, all four 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$:
87	Qwen-rw ($\text{CI}_\text{high} = 0.5991$), Qwen-cont (0.5712),
88	Pythia (0.5628), and OLMo (0.5596).
89	Permutation tests confirm $p = 0.002$ for all eight boundary comparisons.
90	Together these establish $\Kempirical = 2$ across all tested configurations.
91	
92	The most marginal case is Qwen-cont, where the 1v2 CI lower bound
93	(0.6015) exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.0015.  This narrow margin
94	indicates that $\Kstar = 2$ is robust but not trivially so---continuation-mode
95	generation produces weaker depth artifacts than rewrite mode, pushing the
96	boundary closer to the detection threshold.
97	
98	The absolute 1v2 $\auc$ varies across models:
99	Qwen-rw (0.6955) $>$ Pythia (0.6539) $>$ OLMo (0.6145) $\approx$ Qwen-cont (0.6112).
100	Notably, the spread due to generation mode within a single model
101	(Qwen-rw vs.\ Qwen-cont: $\Delta = 8.4$\,pp) exceeds the spread
102	across models in the same mode
103	(Pythia vs.\ OLMo: $\Delta = 3.9$\,pp),
104	suggesting that generation protocol is a stronger determinant
105	of detectability than model identity.
106	We examine both factors in Sections~\ref{sec:transfer}
107	and~\ref{sec:generation_mode}.
108	
109	Beyond the $\Kstar$ boundary, depth discrimination deteriorates
110	rapidly.
111	OLMo shows nonsignificant permutation $p$-values at 3v4
112	($p = 0.064$) and 4v5 ($p = 0.232$), indicating that depth
113	classification beyond generation~2 is indistinguishable from
114	random for this model.
115	Pythia retains marginal effects at these depths
116	($p = 0.006$ and $p = 0.008$, respectively),
117	while Qwen-cont shows weak but detectable discrimination through
118	3v4 ($p = 0.002$) that fades at 4v5 ($p = 0.006$).
119	
120	%% ====================================================================
121	\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}
122	\label{sec:transfer}
123	
124	To assess whether depth signals are properties of the text itself
125	rather than artifacts of a specific generator, we train classifiers
126	on one model's outputs and evaluate on another's.
127	Table~\ref{tab:transfer_matrix} shows the full
128	$4 \times 4$ transfer accuracy matrix for 6-class ordinal depth
129	classification.
130	
131	\begin{table}[t]
132	\centering
133	\small
134	\caption{Cross-model transfer accuracy (6-class ordinal
135	classification).  Diagonal entries (bold): within-model accuracy.
136	Off-diagonal: cross-model transfer.  Retention is computed as
137	off-diagonal accuracy divided by the diagonal entry of the training
138	model.}
139	\label{tab:transfer_matrix}
140	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
141	\toprule
142	Train $\downarrow$ / Test $\rightarrow$
143	  & Qwen-rw & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-cont \\
144	\midrule
145	Qwen-rw
146	  & \textbf{0.4229} & 0.2590 & 0.2653 & 0.3466 \\
147	Pythia
148	  & 0.2718 & \textbf{0.3856} & 0.3531 & 0.3287 \\
149	OLMo
150	  & 0.2768 & 0.3450 & \textbf{0.3822} & 0.3244 \\
151	Qwen-cont
152	  & 0.3440 & 0.3284 & 0.3112 & \textbf{0.3875} \\
153	\bottomrule
154	\end{tabular}
155	\end{table}
156	
157	\begin{figure}[t]
158	\centering
159	\includegraphics[width=0.85\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_transfer_heatmap.pdf}
160	\caption{Cross-model transfer heatmap (6-class ordinal accuracy).
161	Rows: training model; columns: test model.
162	Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo (both continuation mode) shows high
163	mutual transfer (91--92\% accuracy retention), while Qwen-rewrite
164	transfers poorly to continuation-mode models (61--63\%).
165	Diagonal entries are within-model baselines.}
166	\label{fig:transfer_heatmap}
167	\end{figure}
168	
169	Two principal findings emerge.
170	First, transfer between continuation-mode models is high.
171	Pythia$\to$OLMo retains 91--92\% of within-model accuracy, and
172	the reverse direction is comparable
173	(85--86\% retention by Kendall $\tau$).
174	The accuracy-based retention of 91--92\% is complemented by the
175	$\tau$-based retention of 85--86\%, indicating that not only
176	classification accuracy but also the relative depth ordering of
177	predictions is largely preserved.
178	Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$Pythia also transfers well
179	(83--85\% accuracy retention),
180	and Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$OLMo achieves 80--85\%.
181	These retention rates indicate that a substantial fraction of
182	the depth signal---on the order of 70--85\%---is text-intrinsic
183	rather than tied to a specific generator.
184	
185	Second, Qwen-rewrite exhibits catastrophic transfer failure.
186	Classifiers trained on Qwen-rewrite retain only 61--63\% of
187	within-model accuracy when evaluated on Pythia or OLMo
188	(45--50\% by $\tau$).
189	The reverse direction performs comparably poorly.
190	This confirms that rewrite-mode classifiers rely on generation
191	artifacts that do not generalize across models, in contrast
192	to Qwen-cont, which achieves 80--85\% retention to the same targets.
193	
194	At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model pairwise $\auc$ exceeds 0.96
195	for all model pairs, confirming that the human-vs.-synthetic
196	distinction is universally transferable regardless of generator
197	or mode.
198	The transfer degradation concentrates at deeper boundaries
199	(1v2 and beyond), where model- and mode-specific factors dominate.
200	
201	The aggregate picture is one of modest cross-model loss:
202	mean pairwise $\auc$ is 0.6099 within-model versus 0.5905
203	cross-model.
204	This gap is driven primarily by Qwen-rewrite; among
205	continuation-mode pairs the within/cross difference narrows
206	further.
207	
208	%% ====================================================================
209	\subsection{Feature Degradation Ordering}
210	\label{sec:feature_degradation}
211	
212	If depth signals are text-intrinsic, different generators should
213	rely on the same features in the same order.
214	We test this by computing single-feature $\auc$ rankings
215	independently for each model and comparing them via rank
216	correlation.
217	
218	\begin{table}[t]
219	\centering
220	\small
221	\caption{Top-3 features by single-feature $\auc$ ranking for each
222	model configuration.
223	Features shared across all three continuation-mode models are in bold.
224	Qwen-rewrite's top feature (\texttt{freq\_entropy}) is mode-specific.
225	Spearman $\rho$ (continuation-mode pairs): Pythia--OLMo 0.95,
226	Pythia--Qwen-cont 0.9143, OLMo--Qwen-cont 0.85.}
227	\label{tab:top_features}
228	\begin{tabular}{cllll}
229	\toprule
230	Rank & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-rw & Qwen-cont \\
231	\midrule
232	1
233	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}}
234	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_std}}
235	  & \texttt{freq\_entropy}
236	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}} \\
237	2
238	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d2\_std}}
239	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}}
240	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_std}}
241	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_std}} \\
242	3
243	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_std}}
244	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d2\_std}}
245	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}}
246	  & \textbf{\texttt{surp\_d2\_std}} \\
247	\bottomrule
248	\end{tabular}
249	\end{table}
250	
251	Among continuation-mode models, single-feature $\auc$ rankings
252	are highly correlated:
253	Pythia vs.\ OLMo $\rho = 0.95$,
254	Pythia vs.\ Qwen-cont $\rho = 0.9143$,
255	OLMo vs.\ Qwen-cont $\rho = 0.85$
256	(all $\rho \geq 0.85$).
257	The top-3 features---\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}, \texttt{surp\_std},
258	and \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}---are shared (up to ordering) across
259	all three continuation-mode configurations
260	(Table~\ref{tab:top_features}).
261	All three measure variability of surprisal or its derivatives,
262	capturing the \emph{heterogeneity} of token-level predictability
263	across the text.
264	That these features degrade in a shared order across generators
265	suggests a common mechanism: each generation step smooths the
266	token-level surprisal landscape, reducing its variance in a
267	model-independent fashion.
268	
269	Qwen-rewrite diverges: its top-ranked feature is
270	\texttt{freq\_entropy}, a lexical diversity measure absent from
271	the continuation-mode top-3 for any model.
272	This corroborates the transfer results in
273	Section~\ref{sec:transfer}---rewrite-mode classifiers learn
274	partly from instruction-following artifacts rather than the
275	shared surprisal-based signals.
276	
277	Kendall $\tau$ provides a complementary, more conservative
278	perspective:
279	Pythia vs.\ OLMo $\tau = 0.733$,
280	Pythia vs.\ Qwen-cont $\tau = 0.695$,
281	OLMo vs.\ Qwen-cont $\tau = 0.543$.
282	Cross-mode correlations are lower:
283	Pythia vs.\ Qwen-rw $\tau = 0.467$,
284	OLMo vs.\ Qwen-rw $\tau = 0.429$.
285	
286	\paragraph{Limitation.}
287	The high Spearman $\rho$ characterizes the \emph{aggregate}
288	feature ranking, but at the depth-pair level the agreement
289	weakens: $\tau \approx 0.37$ at the 1v2 boundary.
290	This means that while the overall importance ordering is shared,
291	the relative contribution of individual features at the
292	discrimination boundary---where precision matters most---varies
293	across models.
294	We view this as a genuine limitation of the text-intrinsic
295	interpretation and a direction for future investigation.
296	
297	%% ====================================================================
298	\subsection{Generation Mode Effect}
299	\label{sec:generation_mode}
300	
301	Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct provides a controlled comparison of generation
302	modes: rewrite (instruction-based paraphrasing) and continuation
303	(prompt truncation), as defined in Section~3.
304	Both share the same model weights, isolating the effect of
305	generation protocol on depth detectability.
306	
307	Rewrite mode yields higher 1v2 $\auc$ than continuation:
308	0.6955 vs.\ 0.6112, a difference of $+$8.4 percentage points.
309	The advantage persists at 2v3
310	(0.5893 vs.\ 0.5609, $\Delta = +$2.8\,pp)
311	and narrows at 3v4
312	(0.5435 vs.\ 0.5409, $\Delta = +$0.3\,pp),
313	with both modes converging toward chance at deeper levels.
314	The amplified detectability under rewrite mode is consistent
315	with instruction-following introducing systematic deviations
316	from the source text's style---additional artifacts that are
317	discriminable but mode-specific rather than text-intrinsic.
318	
319	Transfer between modes is asymmetric.
320	A classifier trained on Qwen-cont and evaluated on Qwen-rw
321	retains 89\% of within-model accuracy
322	(0.3440 vs.\ 0.3875 diagonal),
323	whereas the reverse direction---Qwen-rw trained,
324	Qwen-cont tested---retains 82\%
325	(0.3466 vs.\ 0.4229 diagonal).
326	The direction of the asymmetry is intuitive:
327	continuation-mode signals form a subset of the information
328	available in rewrite-mode data
329	(which adds instruction-following artifacts on top),
330	so a continuation-trained classifier can partially recognize
331	rewrite-mode outputs but not vice versa.
332	
333	This asymmetry is mirrored in the feature rankings.
334	Qwen-rewrite's top feature (\texttt{freq\_entropy}) is
335	mode-specific and ranks outside the top-3 for every
336	continuation-mode model.
337	Qwen-cont's top feature (\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}) is shared
338	with Pythia and OLMo, confirming that continuation mode
339	captures primarily text-intrinsic depth signals.
340	
341	The practical implication is a detectability--generalizability
342	tradeoff.
343	Rewrite-mode classifiers achieve higher absolute $\auc$ but
344	transfer poorly across models
345	(Qwen-rw$\to$Pythia/OLMo: 61--63\% retention).
346	Continuation-mode classifiers sacrifice 8.4\,pp of within-model
347	$\auc$ but achieve robust cross-model transfer
348	(Qwen-cont$\to$Pythia: 83--85\%).
349	For deployment scenarios requiring model-agnostic depth
350	estimation, continuation-mode features provide a more reliable
351	foundation despite lower raw discriminability.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate generational depth estimation on four model configurations:
Pythia-1.4B and OLMo-1B in continuation mode, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in both rewrite and continuation modes.
All experiments use the OBD-LightGBM classifier with the 12-dimensional feature set described in Section~3.
Each configuration uses a balanced corpus of 500 texts per depth level (generations 0--5).
We organize results around four questions:
(1)~Does $\Kempirical = 2$ hold across configurations?
(2)~Do depth classifiers transfer across models?
(3)~Is the feature degradation ordering model-independent?
(4)~How does generation mode affect detectability?

%% ====================================================================
\subsection{$\Kstar = 2$ Across All Configurations}
\label{sec:kstar_boundary}

Table~\ref{tab:kstar_ci} reports pairwise $\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs
across all four configurations, with bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals
(1{,}000 resamples) and permutation-test $p$-values for the critical 1v2
and 2v3 boundaries.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ for adjacent depth pairs.  Bootstrap 95\% CIs
and permutation $p$-values shown for the $\Kstar$ boundary rows (1v2,
2v3).  $\Kempirical = 2$ requires 1v2 $\text{CI}_\text{low} > \theta$
and 2v3 $\text{CI}_\text{high} < \theta$ with $\theta = 0.60$.
All 0v1 permutation $p = 0.002$.}
\label{tab:kstar_ci}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
 & Qwen-rw & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-cont \\
\midrule
0v1 & 0.9956 & 0.9932 & 0.9970 & 0.9972 \\[4pt]
1v2 & 0.6955 & 0.6539 & 0.6145 & 0.6112 \\
{\footnotesize CI}
  & {\footnotesize [.6859,\,.7041]}
  & {\footnotesize [.6454,\,.6630]}
  & {\footnotesize [.6045,\,.6247]}
  & {\footnotesize [.6015,\,.6213]} \\
{\footnotesize $p$}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002} \\[4pt]
2v3 & 0.5893 & 0.5514 & 0.5496 & 0.5609 \\
{\footnotesize CI}
  & {\footnotesize [.5795,\,.5991]}
  & {\footnotesize [.5417,\,.5628]}
  & {\footnotesize [.5399,\,.5596]}
  & {\footnotesize [.5511,\,.5712]} \\
{\footnotesize $p$}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002}
  & {\footnotesize .002} \\[4pt]
3v4 & 0.5435 & 0.5152 & 0.5091 & 0.5409 \\
4v5 & 0.5340 & 0.5136 & 0.5045 & 0.5141 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The pattern is uniform across all four configurations:
0v1 discrimination is near-perfect ($\auc > 0.99$),
followed by a sharp drop at 1v2 ($\auc$ range: 0.6112--0.6955),
with 2v3 falling below the decision threshold $\theta = 0.60$
($\auc$ range: 0.5496--0.5893).
All subsequent pairs (3v4, 4v5) converge toward chance.
Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay} visualizes this decay.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_auc_decay.pdf}
\caption{Pairwise $\auc$ as a function of depth pair across four model
configurations.  All configurations show a sharp drop between 0v1 and
1v2, with 2v3 and deeper pairs falling below the decision threshold
$\theta = 0.60$ (dashed line).  Error bars: bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
\label{fig:auc_decay}
\end{figure}

For the $\Kstar$ determination, all four 1v2 CI lower bounds exceed
$\theta$: Qwen-rw ($\text{CI}_\text{low} = 0.6859$), Pythia (0.6454),
OLMo (0.6045), and Qwen-cont (0.6015).
Conversely, all four 2v3 CI upper bounds fall below $\theta$:
Qwen-rw ($\text{CI}_\text{high} = 0.5991$), Qwen-cont (0.5712),
Pythia (0.5628), and OLMo (0.5596).
Permutation tests confirm $p = 0.002$ for all eight boundary comparisons.
Together these establish $\Kempirical = 2$ across all tested configurations.

The most marginal case is Qwen-cont, where the 1v2 CI lower bound
(0.6015) exceeds $\theta$ by only 0.0015.  This narrow margin
indicates that $\Kstar = 2$ is robust but not trivially so---continuation-mode
generation produces weaker depth artifacts than rewrite mode, pushing the
boundary closer to the detection threshold.

The absolute 1v2 $\auc$ varies across models:
Qwen-rw (0.6955) $>$ Pythia (0.6539) $>$ OLMo (0.6145) $\approx$ Qwen-cont (0.6112).
Notably, the spread due to generation mode within a single model
(Qwen-rw vs.\ Qwen-cont: $\Delta = 8.4$\,pp) exceeds the spread
across models in the same mode
(Pythia vs.\ OLMo: $\Delta = 3.9$\,pp),
suggesting that generation protocol is a stronger determinant
of detectability than model identity.
We examine both factors in Sections~\ref{sec:transfer}
and~\ref{sec:generation_mode}.

Beyond the $\Kstar$ boundary, depth discrimination deteriorates
rapidly.
OLMo shows nonsignificant permutation $p$-values at 3v4
($p = 0.064$) and 4v5 ($p = 0.232$), indicating that depth
classification beyond generation~2 is indistinguishable from
random for this model.
Pythia retains marginal effects at these depths
($p = 0.006$ and $p = 0.008$, respectively),
while Qwen-cont shows weak but detectable discrimination through
3v4 ($p = 0.002$) that fades at 4v5 ($p = 0.006$).

%% ====================================================================
\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}
\label{sec:transfer}

To assess whether depth signals are properties of the text itself
rather than artifacts of a specific generator, we train classifiers
on one model's outputs and evaluate on another's.
Table~\ref{tab:transfer_matrix} shows the full
$4 \times 4$ transfer accuracy matrix for 6-class ordinal depth
classification.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-model transfer accuracy (6-class ordinal
classification).  Diagonal entries (bold): within-model accuracy.
Off-diagonal: cross-model transfer.  Retention is computed as
off-diagonal accuracy divided by the diagonal entry of the training
model.}
\label{tab:transfer_matrix}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
Train $\downarrow$ / Test $\rightarrow$
  & Qwen-rw & Pythia & OLMo & Qwen-cont \\
\midrule
Qwen-rw
  & \textbf{0.4229} & 0.2590 & 0.2653 & 0.3466 \\
Pythia
  & 0.2718 & \textbf{0.3856} & 0.3531 & 0.3287 \\
OLMo
  & 0.2768 & 0.3450 & \textbf{0.3822} & 0.3244 \\
Qwen-cont
  & 0.3440 & 0.3284 & 0.3112 & \textbf{0.3875} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.85\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_transfer_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Cross-model transfer heatmap (6-class ordinal accuracy).
Rows: training model; columns: test model.
Pythia$\leftrightarrow$OLMo (both continuation mode) shows high
mutual transfer (91--92\% accuracy retention), while Qwen-rewrite
transfers poorly to continuation-mode models (61--63\%).
Diagonal entries are within-model baselines.}
\label{fig:transfer_heatmap}
\end{figure}

Two principal findings emerge.
First, transfer between continuation-mode models is high.
Pythia$\to$OLMo retains 91--92\% of within-model accuracy, and
the reverse direction is comparable
(85--86\% retention by Kendall $\tau$).
The accuracy-based retention of 91--92\% is complemented by the
$\tau$-based retention of 85--86\%, indicating that not only
classification accuracy but also the relative depth ordering of
predictions is largely preserved.
Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$Pythia also transfers well
(83--85\% accuracy retention),
and Qwen-cont$\leftrightarrow$OLMo achieves 80--85\%.
These retention rates indicate that a substantial fraction of
the depth signal---on the order of 70--85\%---is text-intrinsic
rather than tied to a specific generator.

Second, Qwen-rewrite exhibits catastrophic transfer failure.
Classifiers trained on Qwen-rewrite retain only 61--63\% of
within-model accuracy when evaluated on Pythia or OLMo
(45--50\% by $\tau$).
The reverse direction performs comparably poorly.
This confirms that rewrite-mode classifiers rely on generation
artifacts that do not generalize across models, in contrast
to Qwen-cont, which achieves 80--85\% retention to the same targets.

At the 0v1 boundary, cross-model pairwise $\auc$ exceeds 0.96
for all model pairs, confirming that the human-vs.-synthetic
distinction is universally transferable regardless of generator
or mode.
The transfer degradation concentrates at deeper boundaries
(1v2 and beyond), where model- and mode-specific factors dominate.

The aggregate picture is one of modest cross-model loss:
mean pairwise $\auc$ is 0.6099 within-model versus 0.5905
cross-model.
This gap is driven primarily by Qwen-rewrite; among
continuation-mode pairs the within/cross difference narrows
further.

\label{sec:feature_degradation}

If depth signals are text-intrinsic, different generators should
rely on the same features in the same order.
We test this by computing single-feature $\auc$ rankings
independently for each model and comparing them via rank
correlation.

Among continuation-mode models, single-feature $\auc$ rankings
are highly correlated:
Pythia vs.\ OLMo $\rho = 0.95$,
Pythia vs.\ Qwen-cont $\rho = 0.9143$,
OLMo vs.\ Qwen-cont $\rho = 0.85$
(all $\rho \geq 0.85$).
The top-3 features---\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}, \texttt{surp\_std},
and \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}---are shared (up to ordering) across
all three continuation-mode configurations
(Table~\ref{tab:top_features}).
All three measure variability of surprisal or its derivatives,
capturing the \emph{heterogeneity} of token-level predictability
across the text.
That these features degrade in a shared order across generators
suggests a common mechanism: each generation step smooths the
token-level surprisal landscape, reducing its variance in a
model-independent fashion.

Qwen-rewrite diverges: its top-ranked feature is
\texttt{freq\_entropy}, a lexical diversity measure absent from
the continuation-mode top-3 for any model.
This corroborates the transfer results in
Section~\ref{sec:transfer}---rewrite-mode classifiers learn
partly from instruction-following artifacts rather than the
shared surprisal-based signals.

Kendall $\tau$ provides a complementary, more conservative
perspective:
Pythia vs.\ OLMo $\tau = 0.733$,
Pythia vs.\ Qwen-cont $\tau = 0.695$,

The high Spearman $\rho$ characterizes the \emph{aggregate}
feature ranking, but at the depth-pair level the agreement
weakens: $\tau \approx 0.37$ at the 1v2 boundary.
This means that while the overall importance ordering is shared,
the relative contribution of individual features at the
discrimination boundary---where precision matters most---varies
across models.
We view this as a genuine limitation of the text-intrinsic
interpretation and a direction for future investigation.

\subsection{Generation Mode Effect}
\label{sec:generation_mode}

Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct provides a controlled comparison of generation
modes: rewrite (instruction-based paraphrasing) and continuation
(prompt truncation), as defined in Section~3.
Both share the same model weights, isolating the effect of
generation protocol on depth detectability.

Rewrite mode yields higher 1v2 $\auc$ than continuation:
0.6955 vs.\ 0.6112, a difference of $+$8.4 percentage points.
The advantage persists at 2v3
(0.5893 vs.\ 0.5609, $\Delta = +$2.8\,pp)
and narrows at 3v4
(0.5435 vs.\ 0.5409, $\Delta = +$0.3\,pp),
with both modes converging toward chance at deeper levels.
The amplified detectability under rewrite mode is consistent
with instruction-following introducing systematic deviations
from the source text's style---additional artifacts that are
discriminable but mode-specific rather than text-intrinsic.

Transfer between modes is asymmetric.
A classifier trained on Qwen-cont and evaluated on Qwen-rw
retains 89\% of within-model accuracy
(0.3440 vs.\ 0.3875 diagonal),
whereas the reverse direction---Qwen-rw trained,
Qwen-cont tested---retains 82\%
(0.3466 vs.\ 0.4229 diagonal).
The direction of the asymmetry is intuitive:
continuation-mode signals form a subset of the information
available in rewrite-mode data
(which adds instruction-following artifacts on top),
so a continuation-trained classifier can partially recognize
rewrite-mode outputs but not vice versa.

This asymmetry is mirrored in the feature rankings.
Qwen-rewrite's top feature (\texttt{freq\_entropy}) is
mode-specific and ranks outside the top-3 for every
continuation-mode model.
Qwen-cont's top feature (\texttt{surp\_d1\_std}) is shared
with Pythia and OLMo, confirming that continuation mode
captures primarily text-intrinsic depth signals.

The practical implication is a detectability--generalizability
tradeoff.
Rewrite-mode classifiers achieve higher absolute $\auc$ but
transfer poorly across models
(Qwen-rw$\to$Pythia/OLMo: 61--63\% retention).
Continuation-mode classifiers sacrifice 8.4\,pp of within-model
$\auc$ but achieve robust cross-model transfer
(Qwen-cont$\to$Pythia: 83--85\%).
For deployment scenarios requiring model-agnostic depth
estimation, continuation-mode features provide a more reliable
foundation despite lower raw discriminability.

Input:  features.csv (30000 rows: doc_id, depth, 15 features)

import argparse
import json
import os
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections import Counter
from hashlib import md5

]

    def fit(self, features: np.ndarray, depths: np.ndarray, texts: list = None):
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_weights(self, features: np.ndarray, texts: list = None) -> np.ndarray:

## 审查报告 — Method Section (docs/paper/method.tex)

**结论**: CRITICAL

### 发现

- [severity: critical] **特征表（Table 1）与代码不符**：Table 1 列出的 tail_ratio、top10_mass、repetition_rate 三个特征在代码中不存在。代码实际使用的 surp_d1_skew、ttr、low_freq_ratio 三个特征在 Table 1 中缺失。证据：`exp006_filtering_strategies.py:26-32` FEATURE_COLS 定义了 15 个特征，其中这 3 个与论文不符。审稿人若对照代码必发现此矛盾，直接质疑实验可复现性。

- [severity: warning] **CV 方法描述错误**：论文第 164 行称 "5-fold stratified cross-validation"，但代码全部使用 GroupKFold（证据：run_pipeline.py:428,464,528; bootstrap_ci.py:14,55; run_exp010:95; run_exp013:102），无任何 StratifiedKFold。GroupKFold 按 seed document 分组是正确的设计选择（防止同一 seed 的不同深度分散到训练/测试集造成泄漏），但称之为 "stratified" 是不准确的。建议改为 "5-fold group cross-validation (grouped by seed document)"。

- [severity: warning] **DPI 推导逻辑跳跃**：第 28-31 行声称 "I(Y_k; Y_{k+1}) → 0 as k grows"，理由是 I(X;Y_k) 单调递减有下界所以收敛。但 I(X;Y_k) 收敛不蕴含 I(Y_k;Y_{k+1}) → 0。后者是相邻代之间的互信息，在稳态下等于信道容量（>0，因为 nucleus sampling 有随机性）。K* 存在的正确论证应基于 Markov 链收敛到平稳分布（使相邻代的**边缘分布**趋同），而非 DPI。信息论背景的审稿人会抓住这个逻辑漏洞。建议修正论证路径。

## 审查报告 — Experiments Section (docs/paper/experiments_c1.tex)

**结论**: CRITICAL

### 发现

- [severity: critical] **模型名称错误**：第 5 行写 "Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct"，实际为 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct。证据：run_pipeline.py:4 ("Generates recursive depth chains from C4 seed data using Qwen2.5-1.5B") 及 611 行 (default="/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct")。与 method.tex Table 2 也矛盾（Table 2 正确写了 1.5B）。

- [severity: critical] **特征维度错误**：第 6 行写 "12-dimensional feature set"，实际为 15 维。证据：exp006_filtering_strategies.py:26-32 FEATURE_COLS 包含 15 个特征，method.tex Section 3 也说 "15-dimensional"。两个章节自相矛盾。

- [severity: critical] **样本数量错误**：第 7 行写 "500 texts per depth level"，实际为 5,000。证据：data_exp001_pythia/features.csv 有 30,001 行 = 30,000 数据行 = 5,000 × 6 深度；method.tex 明确写 "5,000 documents" (N=5,000)。差一个数量级。

- [severity: warning] **Qwen-cont 0v1 p-value 无数据支撑**：Table 3 脚注称 "All 0v1 permutation p = 0.002"，但 registry exp_007 中 qwen_cont 0v1 的 perm_p = null（未计算）。虽然 AUC > 0.997 几乎确定 p < 0.002，但论文不应在缺少实际数据的情况下做此断言。建议补跑 Qwen-cont 0v1 permutation test 或标注为推断值。

- [severity: warning] **method 与 experiments 数值不一致**：method.tex 第 182 行用 Qwen-rw 1v2 AUC = 0.6957、Qwen-cont = 0.6114（来自 mvp/exp_017），experiments_c1 用 0.6955 和 0.6112（来自 exp_007 bootstrap）。差异仅 0.0002，但两个章节引用不同实验的数值容易被审稿人质疑一致性。建议统一到 exp_007（OBD-LightGBM）数据源。

- [severity: warning] **"70-85% text-intrinsic" 推断过强**：第 183 行称 "a substantial fraction of the depth signal—on the order of 70-85%—is text-intrinsic"，依据是 transfer accuracy retention。但 transfer accuracy retention ≠ 信号分解比例，这两者的数学关系未建立。审稿人可能质疑此推断。建议弱化为 "transfer retention of 80-92% suggests a large text-intrinsic component" 而不给出具体比例。

Table 3（pairwise AUC + CI + p-value）：与 registry exp_007 逐项核对，**全部一致** ✓
Table 4（transfer matrix）：与 registry exp_013 逐项核对，**全部一致** ✓
Table 5（feature ranking + correlation）：与 registry exp_005 逐项核对，**全部一致** ✓

### 积极评价

- [severity: info] 叙事结构清晰：四个研究问题组织合理，结果与问题一一对应
- [severity: info] Limitation 段落（§4.3 末尾）诚实披露 τ≈0.37 @1v2 boundary 的弱点，增强可信度
- [severity: info] Detectability-generalizability tradeoff framing（§4.4 末段）论据充分、逻辑连贯
- [severity: info] 最边缘案例 Qwen-cont CI_lower=0.6015 的分析（§4.1）是正确的透明度实践

\subsection{Feature Extraction}
\label{sec:features}

We characterize each document with a 15-dimensional statistical feature vector, organized into five groups (Table~\ref{tab:features}).
All features are computed from token-level surprisal values and frequency statistics obtained via an external scorer model on the tokenized text.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{The 15-dimensional feature set for generational depth estimation.}
\label{tab:features}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
\textbf{Group} & \textbf{Feature} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Surprisal\\moments}}
  & \texttt{surp\_mean}      & Mean token surprisal \\
  & \texttt{surp\_std}       & Std.\ dev.\ of token surprisal \\
  & \texttt{surp\_skew}      & Skewness of surprisal dist. \\
  & \texttt{surp\_kurtosis}  & Kurtosis of surprisal dist. \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Surprisal\\derivatives}}
  & \texttt{surp\_d1\_mean}  & Mean 1st-order surprisal diff. \\
  & \texttt{surp\_d1\_std}   & Std.\ dev.\ of 1st-order diff. \\
  & \texttt{surp\_d2\_mean}  & Mean 2nd-order surprisal diff. \\
  & \texttt{surp\_d2\_std}   & Std.\ dev.\ of 2nd-order diff. \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Frequency\\diversity}}
  & \texttt{freq\_entropy}   & Token frequency entropy \\
  & \texttt{freq\_kurtosis}  & Kurtosis of token frequencies \\
  & \texttt{hapax\_ratio}    & Fraction of hapax legomena \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Tail-\\thinning}}
  & \texttt{tail\_ratio}     & Token mass below 10th pctl. \\
  & \texttt{top10\_mass}     & Prob.\ mass of top-10 tokens \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{\parbox{2.2cm}{Self-\\similarity}}
  & \texttt{self\_bleu}       & Intra-document $n$-gram overlap \\
  & \texttt{repetition\_rate} & Fraction of repeated $n$-grams \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The first two groups capture the distribution and dynamics of token-level surprisal: moments summarize the shape of the surprisal distribution, while derivatives measure its local variability across token positions.
Frequency diversity features quantify lexical richness.
Tail-thinning features capture the well-documented phenomenon whereby recursive generation concentrates probability mass on high-frequency tokens, thinning the distribution tail \cite{shumailov2024collapse, dohmatob2024model}.
Self-similarity features detect the increased repetitiveness characteristic of deeper generations.

We use hand-crafted statistical features rather than learned representations for three reasons: (1) they are directly interpretable, enabling degradation ordering analysis across model families; (2) they transfer across generators without retraining the feature extractor; and (3) they permit attribution of discriminative power to specific text properties, which is essential for understanding \emph{how} the depth signal degrades.

- [severity: critical] **模型大小错误**。第5行写"Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct"，但代码 run_pipeline.py:4,611 确认模型为 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct，method.tex Table 2 也写 1.5B。7B 是完全错误的型号。

- [severity: critical] **特征维度错误**。第6行写"12-dimensional feature set"，但 method.tex §3.2 写"15-dimensional"，代码 FEATURE_COLS 也是 15 维。12 和 15 的矛盾审稿人一眼就能发现。

- [severity: critical] **样本数量错误**。第7行写"500 texts per depth level"，但实际数据 data_exp001_pythia/features.csv 有 30,001 行（30,000 数据 + 1 header = 5,000 per depth × 6 depths），method.tex §3.5 也写"5,000 documents"。500 vs 5,000 差了一个数量级。

- [severity: warning] **Qwen-cont 0v1 permutation p 无数据支撑**。Table 3 caption 声称"All 0v1 permutation p = 0.002"，但 registry exp_007 中 qwen_cont 0v1 的 perm_p = null。虽然以 AUC=0.9972 推断 p≤0.002 合理，但论文应基于实际数据而非推断。建议补跑或标注。

- [severity: warning] **跨章节 AUC 数值不一致**。method.tex §3.6 第182行引用 Qwen-rw 1v2 AUC=0.6957（来自 mvp, multiclass LightGBM）和 Qwen-cont=0.6114（来自 exp_017），而 experiments_c1.tex 用 0.6955 和 0.6112（来自 exp_007, OBD-LightGBM bootstrap）。同一论文两个章节对相同量使用不同值。虽差异微小（~0.0002），审稿人会质疑为何两处不一致。建议统一使用 exp_007（OBD-LightGBM）数据。

**B. 叙事逻辑**

- [severity: warning] **"70-85% text-intrinsic"推断逻辑跳跃**。第183行从 transfer accuracy retention 80-92% 推断"70-85% of the depth signal is text-intrinsic"。Transfer retention 衡量的是分类器在新数据上的准确率保持比例，不等于信号的内在比例。低 retention 可能源于分类器过拟合而非信号差异。建议改为更保守的表述："suggesting that the majority of the depth signal generalizes across generators" 而非给出具体百分比。

- [severity: info] **Limitation 段落（§4.3 第286-295行）**。τ~0.37 at 1v2 boundary 的诚实披露是加分项，显著降低审稿人对"model-independent"过度声称的攻击力度。建议保留。

**C. 审稿人攻击面**

- [severity: warning] **模型规模局限**。所有模型 ≤1.5B 参数。审稿人必问：K* 在 7B/70B 级模型上是否仍为 2？当前论文未讨论此局限。建议在 §4 末尾或 Conclusion 中明确标注 scale limitation 并讨论预期方向。

- [severity: info] **Permutation p-value 分辨率**。所有关键边界的 p=0.002 = 1/500（500 次 permutation 的最小可能值）。这意味着真实 p 可能远小于 0.002，但当前分辨率无法区分 p=0.001 和 p=0.0001。不影响结论但审稿人可能评论。如果要强化，对 1v2 边界增加到 5000 或 10000 次 permutation 可提供更精确的 p 值。

**D. 数字交叉验证**

以下所有值与 registry 完全一致（逐一核对）：
- Table 3 全部 20 个 AUC 值 ✓（exp_007）
- Table 3 全部 8 组 CI bound ✓
- Table 3 全部 p-values ✓（除 Qwen-cont 0v1 如上所述）
- Table 4 全部 16 个 transfer accuracy 值 ✓（exp_013）
- Table 5 全部 12 个 top-3 feature 排名 ✓（exp_005）
- 正文中 Spearman ρ (0.95, 0.9143, 0.85) 和 Kendall τ (0.733, 0.695, 0.543, 0.467, 0.429) 全部 ✓
- 正文中 transfer retention 百分比全部 ✓
- 正文中 mean pairwise AUC (within 0.6099, cross 0.5905) ✓

### 建议
1. **立即修正三个 CRITICAL 错误**：7B→1.5B, 12→15, 500→5,000
2. 统一两个章节的 AUC 数值来源（建议全用 exp_007 OBD-LightGBM）
3. 补跑 Qwen-cont 0v1 permutation test 或修改 caption 措辞
4. 软化"70-85% text-intrinsic"的措辞
5. 添加模型规模 limitation 讨论
